parts.title: Part 1
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.question: Where's the girl going this afternoon?
Which is the boy's new desk?
options: desk with two drawers on the left and three shelves on the right
desk with shelves on the left and drawers on the right

items.question: How will they get to their tennis class?
Which woman is Laura's new English teacher?
options: woman with short dark hair and glasses

items.question: What might Harry do if it rains on Saturday?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Are you coming shopping with me and Mom this afternoon?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: To buy your new skateboard? I'd love to, but I'm meeting my classmate Susan. <u>We're going to see that new Japanese cartoon.</u>

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: OK, no problem. Mom can help me choose a skateboard.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: And Mom wants to go to the new café in Bridge Street.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Great! They sell fantastic cakes!

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Mum's bought me a desk for my bedroom, Aunt Barbara!

script.speaker: Aunt
script.text: Yes. She was looking at one online with four drawers. Did she get that one?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: <u>Mine's got two drawers on the left and three shelves on the right.</u>

script.speaker: Aunt
script.text: That's good – you've got lots of books and things. Can I go upstairs and look at it?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Sure!

script.speaker: Boy 1
script.text: Are we going to go to our tennis class by bike today? The weather's good.

script.speaker: Boy 2
script.text: Yes, it's sunny but not too hot. But I've got a problem with my back wheel, so I'd prefer to go by bus.

script.speaker: Boy 1
script.text: <u>Or we could walk. It's not far.</u>

script.speaker: Boy 2
script.text: Good idea. My dad says he'll fix my bike next weekend.

script.speaker: Laura
script.text: Mum, you see the woman outside the bookshop? That's my new English teacher.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: The woman with long dark hair? She looks like your Aunt Suzanna.

script.speaker: Laura
script.text: But Aunt Suzanna's got blonde hair! Anyway, <u>it's the other woman, with short dark hair and glasses.</u>

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Oh, she looks really friendly!

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Now, I want to tell you about a new school music club. It'll begin on the fifteenth of September and there will be classes once a week until December the eighteenth.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Let me check the day… Because there's the sports club on Wednesdays, <u>the music club will be on Thursdays</u>.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: It'll be after school. Your last lessons finish at ten to four and you can have a break before the music club because <u>it starts at twenty past four</u> and ends at five o'clock.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Here's some information about the teacher. His name's <u>Mr Taylor</u>. I'll spell that for you T-A-Y-L-O-R. You don't know him because he's new.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: If your parents would like to phone him, he's happy for me to give you his phone number. It's <u>zero-double seven-nine, three-eight-six, five-two-one</u>.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Oh, you need to know where to go for the club. <u>It's going to be in the library</u>. Use the doors next to the art room because the other doors won't be open then.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear Luis talking to his friend Charlotte about a computer game.

items.question: Where did Luis first find out about the game?
Who does Luis want to play the game with?
How long did Charlotte play the game for last Saturday?
Which part of the game does Luis like best?

script.speaker: Luis
script.text: Charlotte! I've got the computer game called Green Space.

script.speaker: Charlotte
script.text: Where did you find out about it, Luis?

script.speaker: Luis
script.text: <u>I borrowed a magazine from a schoolfriend and there was an ad for it.</u> I asked my mum and she bought it for me from their website.

script.speaker: Charlotte
script.text: I really like that game. It's not new, but it's my favourite game because <u>it isn't easy</u>. I play it a lot, which is strange because it's not funny at all! Who are you going to play it with?

script.speaker: Luis
script.text: Well, my brother's too busy studying, and my cousin Amy only likes board games. But <u>my granddad has lots of time, so I want to play with him</u>. How long do you usually play it for?

script.speaker: Charlotte
script.text: When I was sick last Wednesday, I played for an hour and a half. Then, on Friday, an hour. And <u>on Saturday, three quarters of an hour</u>! Which part do you like best?

script.speaker: Luis
script.text: Crossing the river's really good, but <u>the bit I enjoy most is finding something to eat</u>. The part about building a hut's my least favourite.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.question: You will hear two friends talking about shopping. What did the boy buy yesterday?
You will hear a teacher talking to a student called Lyn. Why didn't Lyn come to school yesterday?
options: She arrived back late from holiday.

items.question: You will hear a boy talking about surfing. How did he learn to surf?
You will hear a girl talking about her day at school. Which subject did she like best?
You will hear two brothers talking about last night. Why did they both sleep badly?
options: There were noises in the street.
They were excited about going on holiday.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: I'm glad I got the school book I wanted yesterday.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Yes, my mum had already bought that and a new magazine for me. <u>Everyone thinks the gloves I got yesterday are cool, too.</u>

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: The T-shirt I liked was really colourful!

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: But nearly one hundred pounds!

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: I know. Let's buy some snacks now. We can eat them during break at school.

script.speaker: Lyn
script.text: Mr Jones, could I ask you about the tennis match on Saturday?

script.speaker: Mr Jones
script.text: Of course, Lyn. You missed class yesterday. Do you feel better?

script.speaker: Lyn
script.text: Oh, I wasn't ill. We were camping in Switzerland for a week and <u>our flight was cancelled on Sunday. We flew on Monday instead.</u>

script.speaker: Mr Jones
script.text: Oh, OK. So, next Saturday's really important. If we win, we'll win the championship!

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: When I started surfing, I went to the beach with friends and tried and tried, but I didn't seem to improve. Then, I saw that someone was organising lessons, but they were on Fridays when I play football. In the end, <u>I found a website with a famous surfer showing people the best way to learn</u>. That's what helped me.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: School was great today. First, we had a lesson about oceans and the average water temperature in each one. But <u>the most interesting lesson was about bees – how they live together and how they develop from eggs to adults</u>. In another lesson, we read part of a novel and, for homework, we can write either a story or an article.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: I'm tired this morning. I didn't sleep well.

script.speaker: Nathan
script.text: Neither did I. <u>Let's ask Dad to turn down the heating in our room.</u>

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: Yes, that was the problem. I can hear him outside. I think he's packing the car so that we are ready to go camping.

script.speaker: Nathan
script.text: I can hear Mum playing music downstairs. Let's ask her about the heating.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: Yeah.

parts.title: Part 5
parts.instructions: You will hear Lucas talking to his mum about the jobs his friends want to do. What job does each friend want to do?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: Mum, we talked about different jobs in class today and I'm surprised about the jobs some of my friends want to do.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: What do you want to do?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: <u>You know I love planes, so I'd like to fly them for my job.</u>

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Great idea. What job does Tyler want to do?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: He wants to work at the hospital. His mum's a receptionist there, but <u>he wants to take care of people's teeth!</u>

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: That's a good job. Ava wants to be a sports coach, doesn't she?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: Not now, <u>she wants to show tourists round different towns.</u>

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Oh. And Mark?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: <u>He's always helping his dad repair cars.</u> Remember, his dad's got a garage? And that's what he wants to do.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: He'll be good at that. Does Victoria know what she wants to do?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: Yes, <u>to write articles for a newspaper</u>. She wrote a good story about an actor for English last week.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Great! What about Bobby?

script.speaker: Lucas
script.text: <u>He wants to be in plays and work in theatres all over the world.</u>

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: He was good in the school play about a hospital.
